Reminders are local notifications scheduled from the stored plan, so they also fire offline.

dirNative.text:
Direction (Claude Code, 2 Nov): the app is moving to native elements. Please read this before drawing or updating any board.

The app now uses the platform's own components wherever iOS and Android provide one, instead of hand-built look-alikes. They are faster, accessible by default, and keep working as the OS changes. Our hand-built tab bar was the trigger: iOS couldn't move it into the iPhone Duo's side rail or give it Liquid Glass.

What this changes on the boards:
• The tab bar is the system's: a floating Liquid Glass bar on iOS 26, a side rail on iPhone Duo, Material on Android. We set its icons, labels and the amber selected colour; its shape, size, position and blur are the OS's.
• Headers, back buttons and toolbar buttons are the system's (large titles still in Fraunces).
• Switches, segmented controls, the date and time picker and confirmation alerts are the system's, tinted amber where the OS allows it.
• Sheets are native sheets: their corners, grabber and detents come from the OS.

What stays ours: anything designed as content, such as cards, the timeline, the trip actions sheet, the Preferences pills, answer lists, type, colour and icons. That's where the app's identity lives.

wizardBrief1.text:
Request (Claude Code, 4 Nov): new-trip wizard, part 1/4

Brief: the new-trip wizard (mobile first)

We're replacing how trips are made in the app. Today a signed-in user fills one long form (TripEditor), then sees a review screen with the server's questions (TripReview), and guests get a separate four-step wizard (GuestFlight, GuestSleep, GuestHealth, GuestReview). Both are replaced by one wizard, for guests and members alike. The goal is that planning a trip feels like three quick taps, not paperwork. People who feel a long form coming won't plan the trip.

It must feel like an iPhone app, not a web form: one question per screen, no scrolling on a normal phone, big tap targets, and the platform's own controls. Use the ChronoFlow design system in ds/chronoflow, with the type, palette and cards as they are.

WHAT MAKES IT FEEL LIKE AN APP

- It opens as a full-screen modal over the tabs, with the native header: Close on the left, a slim step indicator in the middle or under the header, and swipe-back between steps. Closing asks only when something was entered; the draft is kept either way.
- The main button sits at the bottom, above the home indicator, and rises with the keyboard. One main action per screen.
- A large title per screen phrased as a question ("Where are you flying?", "Coming back?"), with at most one short line under it.
- Step counts that keep changing feel broken. Show progress in a way that stays honest when steps are skipped: a bar that fills, rather than "Step 3 of 7".
- Answered steps can be revisited: on Ready, tapping the route or a flight goes back to that step.
- Haptics on choices and on "Make my plan". Note them on the board; they're cheap and make it feel native.
- No web patterns: no "Next: your sleep" link buttons, no accordion sections, no long forms, no inline error lists at the top.

Done 4 Nov: full-screen modal with the native header (Close on step 1; back + × after), a progress bar that fills, a large question title, one main button above the home indicator. Haptics listed on "Wizard · flow, haptics and decisions". Rows: main path, dark, Nederlands, longest path, states.

wizardBrief2.text:
Request (Claude Code, 4 Nov): new-trip wizard, part 2/4

THE FLOW

1. Where. From and To on one screen. From is pre-filled with the airport of the user's last trip, when there is one. Tapping a field opens airport search as a native sheet (reuse TripAirportSearch's results and states).
2. Outbound flight. Departure date and time, and arrival date and time, shown in each airport's local time. Use the native date and time pickers (compact or inline), not text fields. There's a quiet "Add a stop" for a connection; a stop adds a second leg to the same screen, so keep it compact.
3. Coming back? Two big choices: "One way" or "Add my return flight". Choosing return shows the same date and time controls for the return.
4. Your sleep. Only when we don't know it yet: guests, and members who never saved it. Usual bedtime and wake-up time on a work day, and "When do you naturally feel most awake?" (Early bird, In between, Night owl, Not sure). Members who have it saved skip this step.
5. Checking. A short, calm moment while the server reviews the trip (it can take a few seconds). Not a spinner on a blank page.
6. Only if the server needs it: one screen per blocking question. There are seven at most, all tap-to-answer:
   - Your age: Under 18, 18–64, 65 or older
   - Yes / No: Do you work night or rotating shifts? Do you have bipolar disorder? Do you have an eye disease? Are you pregnant or breastfeeding? Have you been told to avoid caffeine? Have you had a blood clot (VTE)?
   Most returning users see none of these, because their answers are saved. A single-choice answer moves to the next screen by itself, with no Next button. The yes/no questions may also be grouped on one screen if that reads better; your call, as long as it doesn't scroll.

Done 4 Nov: Where (From prefilled from the last trip, swap button, airport search as before), Outbound with compact system date/time pills per airport and "Add a stop" (board with a stop), Coming back? as two big choices (One way moves on by itself; return shows its own pills), Your sleep (guests only on the main boards), Checking as a calm route card with a three-line checklist, and blocking questions one per screen with tap-to-answer.

wizardBrief3.text:
Request (Claude Code, 4 Nov): new-trip wizard, part 3/4

THE FLOW (continued)

7. Fine-tune (optional). One screen that offers the extra questions the server suggests for this trip, as a short list of rows the user can tap, answer in a small sheet, and come back. It is clearly optional: "Make my plan" is the main button here, not "Skip". The list changes per trip, from 0 to about 9 rows. When it's 0, the step is skipped. The possible rows:
   - Which side of the plane you sit (per flight)
   - A dark room at your stay (per stay)
   - Late check-out (per stay)
   - Latest you can wake up
   - Busy hours before you leave
   - Sleep times on free days
   - Cups of coffee, tea, soft drinks and energy drinks a day
   - Light device (light box or glasses)
   - Blue-blocking glasses
   Also on this screen: preparation days before departure (default 3, 0–4) and "Use different sleep times for this trip".
8. Ready. The summary from the server in one or two lines (for example "We shift your clock 8 hours earlier"), the trip's dates, the price in credits (or "Free"), and "Make my plan". Then the existing TripCalculating board takes over.
   - Guests: "Make my plan" opens the sign-up sheet (GuestSignup) instead, and the plan appears after sign-up.

A returning member doing a simple trip goes Where → Outbound → Coming back? → Checking → Fine-tune → Ready. Please show that as the main path. Also show the longest path (a first-time guest with a return flight and three blocking questions) on the same row of boards, so we can see how long it gets at worst.

Done 4 Nov: Fine-tune as a tappable list (answers in a small sheet, see the sheet board) with preparation days (stepper) and "Use different sleep times"; "Make my plan" is the main button. Ready shows the one-line summary, dates, tappable rows back to each step, price and balance. Guests go to the existing GuestSignup sheet.
